title: The Sigil of Caerlum
premise: Wendell Yarrow, royal food-taster and secret charm-seller in the anti-magic city of Caerlum, discovers her lover Isolde pictured in a century-old book of prophecies as the thirteenth bride promised to the court beneath the mountain. The prophecy demands a soul be surrendered by the moon's thirteenth turn, and Isolde's was sold generations ago by an ancestor who bought the family's fortune with it. Wendell must descend into the under-court, trade on her poison-hardened body and her outlawed small magics, and reclaim the soul before Isolde is claimed. She succeeds only by surrendering her own memories of Isolde as payment, choosing duty to love over the self that remembers it, and the ending hinges on whether a soul once bartered can learn to love again from scratch.
about_author: Mirabel Amberdale is the pseudonym of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval recipe books and poison antidotes before turning to fiction. She writes in a converted lighthouse on the northern coast, where she claims the fog improves her prose.

chapters.title: Chapter 1
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. She samples the king's supper, cataloguing poisons by aftertaste while hiding the ache of immunity built over twelve years. Establishes her double life: taster by day, charm-seller in the night market. Emotional beat: weary competence masking loneliness, and the quiet joy of her courtship with the archivist Isolde.

chapters.title: Chapter 2
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. In the night market she sells luck-knots and headache charms to the desperate, breaking the Edict of Unmaking daily. A customer warns that inquisitors are buying charms as evidence. Emotional beat: the thrill and guilt of outlawed kindness, and first dread of exposure.

chapters.title: Chapter 3
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Cataloguing the restricted archive, Isolde opens a sealed prophecy book and finds her own face inked in the margin, labeled 'the thirteenth bride.' She hides it, then cannot stop returning. Emotional beat: vertigo of self-recognition, the uncanny feeling of being authored by someone else.

chapters.title: Chapter 4
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Isolde shows her the prophecy; the moon is already on its twelfth turn. They research the under-court's bargains and learn Isolde's ancestor sold a soul to buy the family's fortune. Emotional beat: terror converting into resolve; the two lovers pact to fight the prophecy together.

chapters.title: Chapter 5
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Digging through her family's ledgers, Isolde finds the contract: a soul pawned, redeemable only by the debtor's bloodline before the moon completes its turn. Her mother's coldness suddenly reads as fear. Emotional beat: inherited guilt, and the bitter realization her family's comfort was purchased with her.

chapters.title: Chapter 6
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Inquisitor Hale raids the night market; Wendell barely escapes, leaving her stock and a friend to arrest. She realizes the court beneath the mountain and the inquisition may share an interest in her failure. Emotional beat: survivor's guilt and the cost of staying invisible.

chapters.title: Chapter 7
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Following her grandmother's half-remembered rhymes, Wendell finds the old gate to the under-court and bargains passage with a toll-keeper who accepts memories as currency. She pays a minor memory as proof. Emotional beat: dread and awe; the first taste of what descent will truly cost.

chapters.title: Chapter 8
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The under-court revealed: a mirrored inversion of Caerlum where the dead of old bargains serve as courtiers. Wendell poses as a debt-collector to reach the treasury of souls. Emotional beat: uncanny fascination; every courtier was once someone who bargained.

chapters.title: Chapter 9
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. She finds Isolde's soul-shard, a small blue flame labeled in her lover's handwriting. But the treasury warden explains redemption requires payment of equal weight, and souls weigh more than gold. Emotional beat: hope sharpened into desperation.

chapters.title: Chapter 10
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Wendell's POV. Twelve years of tasting: the arsenic breakfasts, the mentor who died teaching her, the slow transformation of her body into a fortress. Reveals why the under-court's magic cannot easily claim her. Emotional beat: reframing her suffering as preparation.

chapters.title: Chapter 11
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The warden offers terms: a soul for a soul, or memories of equal weight to the shard. Wendell begins paying in memories, and each payment unmoors her further from why she came. Emotional beat: the horror of self-erasure as a currency she can actually afford.

chapters.title: Chapter 12
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. While Wendell is below, Isolde stalls the prophecy's fulfillment, deflecting the inquisitors and her own mother, who knows and has always known. Emotional beat: Isolde's quiet ferocity; she refuses to be a bride or a sacrifice.

chapters.title: Chapter 13
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The toll-keeper, once a man who sold his own daughter's soul, helps Wendell navigate the court's politics, confessing his centuries of regret. Emotional beat: a mirror of what Wendell could become; compassion forged in shared damnation.

chapters.title: Chapter 14
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. The inquisition has its own pact with the under-court: souls in exchange for the Edict's power. Hale follows Wendell down, intending to claim Isolde's shard for the crown. Emotional beat: chilling conviction; the antagonist believes he is the loyal one.

chapters.title: Chapter 15
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Paying the final installments, Wendell loses her memories of Isolde one by one, the last being the rainy afternoon they met. She clutches the shard without knowing whose it is. Emotional beat: devastating tenderness; love persisting as instinct after memory is gone.

chapters.title: Chapter 16
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. The moon completes its turn; the under-court's claim activates. Isolde is pulled toward the gate, her mother weeping and confessing at last. Isolde walks in willingly to face whatever holds her soul. Emotional beat: courage without hope of being remembered.

chapters.title: Chapter 17
chapters.summary: Wendell and Isolde's alternating POV. They meet in the treasury, strangers to each other, Wendell holding the shard and Isolde arriving as the bride. The warden demands the bargain be honored either way. Emotional beat: the cruelest irony; they are together and have lost each other.

chapters.title: Chapter 18
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Wendell challenges the contract on a technicality she learned from Isolde's own archival research: the debt was contracted under a name the family no longer bears. She argues Isolde's soul was never validly sold. Emotional beat: intellect as an act of love; fighting with the tools her lover gave her.

chapters.title: Chapter 19
chapters.summary: Hale and Wendell's POV. Hale seizes the shard for the crown, forcing a confrontation in the court of salt. Wendell uses her poison-hardened blood to corrupt the under-court's binding magic, breaking Hale's pact and exposing him to the courtiers he served. Emotional beat: the climax; sacrifice, fury, and the body's loyalty outlasting the mind's.

chapters.title: Chapter 20
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The contract voided, the shard returns to Isolde, but Wendell's memories do not. Isolde carries her home through the tanneries gate as the under-court seals. Emotional beat: grief and gratitude entwined; victory that feels like loss.

chapters.title: Chapter 21
chapters.summary: Isolde's POV. Weeks later, Isolde tends Wendell, who remembers nothing of her. Isolde begins again: telling stories, making tea, teaching her the night market. Wendell, instinctively, ties a luck-knot in Isolde's hair. Emotional beat: fragile, patient hope; love as a practice rather than a memory.

chapters.title: Chapter 22
chapters.summary: Shared POV. On the night market's reopening, Wendell sells charms beside Isolde, the Edict crumbling now that the inquisition's pact is exposed. Wendell says she feels like she's loved Isolde longer than she can prove. Isolde answers: a century of prophecy says so. Emotional beat: resolution; identity rebuilt not from memory but from choice.
